# Continuous Local Screen Recording for AI Agents with Screenpipe

**Source:** https://www.instagram.com/reel/DcJehy0zzAE/ · **Type:** Reel · **Author:** Sean Kochel · **Saved:** 2026-10-13

## Summary

Screenpipe is an open-source tool that records screen and audio 24/7 locally, keeping all captured data private on your device. Local AI agents can query these recorded logs to retrieve meeting transcripts, summarize past conversations, or organize research.

## Transcript and on-screen text

Somebody just open-sourced a tool called screenpipe, and what it allows you to do is record your screen 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and then plug it into your local agents. Now the thing that's cool about this is everything is local. All of these clips are stored locally on your machine, and then you can pass it to any agent that you have. Getting started with it is very easy. All you need to do is come down to their install command and then run `npx screenpipe record`. And from there, it is pretty much good to go out of the box. And just to show you what this looks like in practice: I could come in and I could give a command like 'Use screenpipe to pull the conversation I had between 5-7 PM yesterday with my group members inside of my paid vibe coding community.' And so what this thing did is it went through and it found exactly what conversations we were having, with timestamps of every meaningful piece of that conversation. And then what I asked it to do was zoom in on the conversation we were having about general purpose agents. So we were talking a lot of shit about all of the hype around tools like Hermes, and how people think it'll save them from everything, and they're going to have some personal operating system that manages their entire life, but it's really kind of stupid realistically. And so basically what I said was I needed the transcript because I was going to record a YouTube video about it. And what this did is it went through and it pulled the exact transcript and all of the conversation notes that I was having with people in the group. And I was able to basically take this and then extract all of the points about what we talked about and frame it into a script for my YouTube. So this is one really helpful use case, but there's a lot of use cases obviously. With a tool like this, you can just imagine how powerful it would be if you had something that looked at what you were doing all the time and then allowed you to actually move through and query that. So if you are interested, you can comment screenpipe below and I will send you a link to this repo. On-screen text: Comment "SCREENPIPE" below
